To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the basal activity level of protein kinase A in the wing disc prevents inappropriate dpp and wingless expression and that hedgehog signaling relieves the inhibition by protein kinase A to allow for the expression of dpp and wingloss.
the cAMP-dependent protein kinase A ( PKA) is essential for the proper patterning of the drosophila leg, and that PKA acts by preventing the ectopic activation of the dpp and wg genes.

the Drosophila hh signaling pathway induces the expression of the dpp gene in the posterior compartment of the wing imaginal disc and that the cAMP-dependent protein kinase A (PkA) signaling pathway inhibits dpp and wg gene expression in the anterior wing disc.

the molecular basis of pattern formation in the Drosophila wing imaginal disk.
the mechanisms that control the growth and patterning of the Drosophila limb.
the role of protein kinase A ( PKA ) in the regulation of Hedgehog signaling.

PKA and hh signaling work in concert to regulate the spatial and temporal expression of dpp and wingless in Drosophila limb patterning.
